correctness.rationale: The five displayed Wick-ordered quartics form the whole five-dimensional fourth chaos and have diagonal covariance values 64,48,48,192,192. Polar integration uses E[R^k]=2^k k! and angular character orthogonality to derive the complete fourth-degree coefficient polynomial. An exact integer coefficient comparison independently checks all 70 monomials, and an explicit five-term sum-of-squares identity proves the sharp lower 105 and its exact harmonic-quartic equality subspace. The standard multiple-Wiener-integral product formula and contraction Cauchy–Schwarz give upper 639; equality in the third contraction forces a rank-one fully symmetric tensor and hence one-dimensional Hermite extremizers. The included checker was executed against the new file in this package and returned all five expected success lines. No finite sample is used as a substitute for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The substantive conclusion is the sharp dimension-two fourth-chaos lower moment 105 and exact polynomial deficit with full equality. Nualart–Peccati addresses fourth moments as asymptotic criteria for convergence to Gaussian laws; Malicet et al. gives a general product-of-squares bound whose same-variable specialization is weaker; Latała gives order-only comparison constants. The upper 639 is explicitly attributable to standard contraction estimates, and not asserted as an independently novel general theorem. Targeted published-finding corpus searches returned nearby Rademacher/Walsh and Gaussian-hafnian records but no statement over the real binary fourth Gaussian chaos. Unindexed earlier exact binary-quartic computations remain a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed older invariant-theory identity about binary quartics might imply the same Gaussian-moment deficit after a non-obvious change of variables.
The equality classification and coefficients have not been assessed by an independent mathematical expert.

value.rationale: The five-dimensional fourth Wiener chaos in two Gaussian coordinates is a canonical complete eigenspace for the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck generator and has three nontrivially coupled rotational sectors. Determining the smallest possible standardized fourth moment in that entire space is a natural sharp norm-geometry question not answered by a general fourth-moment CLT or estimates up to constants. The exact 105 constant, full harmonic-quartic equality family and explicit positive deficit show how the radial and second-angular sectors enforce excess fourth moment. The complete interval provides a natural scale for finite-rank Gaussian chaos non-Gaussianity. No broader dimension-general theorem is claimed or required for this exact natural invariant.
